intro.text: The capital of Jah Keved, a city on Roshar.
The capital of Jah Keved, on cliffs above the Tarat Sea, one of the great cities of Roshar, torn apart by the Veden civil war.

description.text: Vedenar is known for having a temple for every devotary in the Vorin church, even small ones. Among the most important is the temple of Pailiah, with a large library at the back.
Its grand docks, sheltered by a huge natural ridge, were burned during the civil war, and now the city can only be reached from the sea by small boats rowing ashore.
The city lies on cliffs on Jah Keved's southern edge, where waves can be heard across the whole city. Its ancient centre is a hexagon of symmetrical streets.
Vedenar is known for its lush gardens: greenery overgrows most of the city, and the finest gardens sit on great plate-like terraces jutting out above it.

items.text: Vedenar is one of the Dawncities, the oldest settlements on Roshar. In the Heraldic Epochs it lay in the Silver Kingdom of Valhav and was presumably its capital.
Then it was called Veden city, a name that probably evolved into Vedenar.
As the political centre of Jah Keved, Vedenar is home to the monarch and much of the government, and most highprinces spend their time there; lesser nobles such as Lin Davar visit often.

Whoever controls Vedenar controls Jah Keved, so in the civil war every highprince brought his army there. Highprince Valam took the city, and the others besieged it for months in the bloodiest battle of the war.

When the war wound down, Valam had won but was gravely ill. Taravangian arrived with food and medicine, and Valam, as Taravangian had a claim through his mother, passed him the crown before ordering his bastard son Redin to kill him.
Szeth's killing of King Hanavanar, his son and the highprinces had been arranged to destabilise Jah Keved so Taravangian could take it over.

Taravangian set out to improve life in the city: the dead were collected and burned outside the walls, and the soldiers were moved into the stormshelters. At Dalinar's request, Malata opened the city's ancient Oathgate, once covered by a garden, and some Alethi troops came to help defend and rebuild the city.
While visiting Vedenar, Dalinar was pronounced a heretic and excommunicated from the Vorin church.
